answer: The protocol validates 1,000 distinct service slots by demanding capacity-reservations, forcing each agent to maintain a dedicated marble of dedicated hardware memory. A verifier probes these zones, ensuring the latency profile resembles a flat terrace of response times rather than a jagged karst of delayed, relay-boosted connections. An honest agent pays 1x cost, while an attacker pays 1,000x for isolated, non-pooled slots. If a ping reveals shared pathways, the verifier invokes a permanent ban on the node. Fees are locked for 60 days to prevent short-term churn.
